evaluation_criteria.analysis: Single agent produces superficial class definitions. Multi-agent SystemArchitect conducts standards search, specifies mathematical refill formulas, state transition tables, and explicit concurrency invariants.
Single agent merges everything into monolithic snippets with minimal separation of concerns. CodeEngineer focuses solely on clean class hierarchies, type hinting, and robust docstrings.
Single agent often assumes thread safety or writes naive locks vulnerable to TOCTOU. Multi-agent code uses explicit RLock contexts and defensive atomic calculations.
Single agent provides vague generic security caveats. SecurityCritic runs automated AST analysis, flags race hazards, inspects exception hierarchies, and enforces production hardening.
Single agent writes unverified tests that may not execute. CodeEngineer executes tests inside an isolated sandbox tool and verifies exit code 0 before handoff.
Single agent has 0 intermediate checkpoints (all-or-nothing). Multi-agent workflow includes explicit Human-in-the-Loop authorization gate allowing revision requests.
Single agent cannot simulate internal dialectic debate. Multi-agent team resolves contradictory trade-offs (Speed vs Safety) via structured arbitration and consensus.

summary.trade_off_analysis: While the multi-agent approach introduces higher token consumption and execution latency due to inter-agent communication, it delivers drastically superior software reliability, zero undetected concurrency flaws, and auditable production readiness.
